en: Covered with or characterised by clouds.
Not transparent or clear.

cloudy.ety: From Middle English cloudy (“cloudy, overcast, gloomy, dark", also "hilly, rocky”), from Old English clūdiġ (“stony, rocky”), equivalent to cloud + -y.

ex.en: All of a sudden, it became cloudy.
ex.ja: 突然、空が曇ってきた。

ex.en: It's getting cloudy. It may rain soon.
ex.ja: くもってきた。やがて雨になるかもしれない。

ex.en: The sky has become a bit cloudy.
ex.ja: 空が少し曇ってきました。

en: Able to be exchanged, one for the other, especially
Able to be exchanged for specie.
A convertible car: a car with a removable or foldable roof able to convert from a closed to open vehicle and back again.
A convertible security: a stock, bond, etc. that can be turned into another (usually common stock) under certain set terms.

convertible.ety: From Old French convertible, from Late Latin convertibilis (“interchangeable”), from Latin convertere (“to turn back, to turn over, to turn around, to turn upside down”), from con- (“with, together”) + vertere (“to turn”), + -ibilis (“-ible: able to”). Equivalent to convert + -ible.

ex.en: I'd like to drive across the USA in a convertible.
ex.ja: コンバーチブルでアメリカを横断したい。

ex.en: I'd like to drive across the USA in a convertible car.
ex.ja: コンバーチブルでアメリカを横断したい。

ex.en: My new Alfa Romeo convertible is light red.
ex.ja: 私の新しいアルファ・ロメオのオープンカーは明るい赤色だ。

note.ja: con（すっかり）+ vert（向ける）+ ible。向きを変えられる →「転換できる・オープンカー（屋根を変えられる車）」。

en: A hemispherical pit created by the impact of a meteorite or other object.
The basin-like opening or mouth of a volcano, through which the chief eruption comes; similarly, the mouth of a geyser, about which a con…
To form craters in a surface.
To collapse catastrophically; to become devastated or completely destroyed.

crater.ety: First coined 1613, from Latin crātēr (“basin”), from Ancient Greek κρᾱτήρ (krātḗr, “mixing-bowl, wassail-bowl”).

ex.en: There are many craters on the moon.
ex.ja: 月にはたくさんのクレーターがある。

en: A person who manages, administers or organizes a collection, either independently or employed by a museum, library, archive or zoo.
One appointed to act as guardian of the estate of a person not legally competent to manage it, or of an absentee; a trustee.

curator.ety: From Latin cūrātor (“one who has care of a thing, a manager, guardian, trustee”), from cūrāre (“to take care of”), from cūra (“care, heed, attention, anxiety, grief”).

en: Synonym of divinity: the state, position, or fact of being a god.
A supernatural divine being; a god or goddess.

deity.ety: From Middle French deité, from Latin deitās.

ex.en: Do you know which deity this temple is dedicated to?
ex.ja: この寺の本尊は何であるか知っていますか。

en: The act of despairing or becoming desperate; a giving up of hope.
A state of despair, or utter hopelessness; abandonment of hope.

desperation.ety: From Middle English desperacion, desperacioun, desperation, disparacion, disperacion, disperacioun, dispiracioune, dysperacioun, from Middle French desperation and its etymon Latin dēspērātiō, dēspērātiōnis. By surface analysis, desperate + -ion.

ex.en: We arrived at that plan out of pure desperation, but the book sold well.
ex.ja: 苦肉の策で企画したんですが、その本はよく売れました。

ex.en: To tell the truth, she gave away all her money to others in desperation.
ex.ja: 実のところ、彼女はやけになって、有り金をみんな人にやってしまったのだ。

ex.en: In a few seconds I would have overcome the desperation threshold.
ex.ja: 後数秒で私は絶望の分岐点を越えるのだ。

en: Causing damage or harm.
Anything harmful.

detrimental.ety: From Medieval Latin *dētrīmentālis, from Latin dētrīmentum (“harm”), from dēterō (“to rub off, wear”), from dē- (“down, away”) + terō (“to rub or grab”).

ex.en: Building up too much stress has a detrimental effect on your health.
ex.ja: ストレスを溜めすぎると健康に悪影響を及ぼす。

note.ja: ラテン語 detrimentum（すり減らすこと）から。de（下に）+ tri（こする）+ ment。→「有害な」。

en: A gastrointestinal disorder characterized by frequent and very soft or watery bowel movements.
The watery or very soft excrement that comes from such bowel movements.

diarrhea.ety:
From Middle English diaria, from Middle French diarrie (French diarrhée), from Late Latin diarrhoea, from Ancient Greek διάρροια (diárrhoia, “through-flowing”), from διά (diá, “through”) + ῥέω (rhéō, “flow”). By surface analysis, dia- + -rrhea. Spelling later altered to resemble the word's Latin and Greek roots.
Displaced native Old English ūtsiht (literally “straining out”).

ex.en: I have a touch of diarrhea.
ex.ja: 下痢気味です。

ex.en: Here's some medicine for diarrhea.
ex.ja: 下痢止めです。

ex.en: I've had diarrhea since yesterday.
ex.ja: 昨日から下痢が続いているんです。

A result of distorting.

distortion.ety: Borrowed from Latin distortio, distortionis, from distortus.

note.ja: dis（離れて）+ tort（ねじる）+ ion。ねじ曲げること →「ゆがみ・歪曲」。

An accumulation, supply, store, or hoard of something.
To reap grain, gather it up, and store it in a granary.
To gather, amass, hoard, as if harvesting grain.

ex.en: The "city pop" genre is now garnering attention across the world.

A member of a Broadway musical chorus line.
To roam around the country like a gypsy.
To perform the gypsy step in contra dancing.

ex.en: She gave clothes to the gypsies out of charity.
ex.ja: 彼女は慈善の気持ちからそのジプシーたちに衣服を与えた。

The state of being humiliated, humbled or reduced to lowliness or submission.

en: The result of being impaired.
A deterioration or weakening.

impairment.ety: From Middle English empeirement, empeyrement, emparement, from Anglo-Norman empairement, emperement, enpeirement, from Old French ampirement, anpirement, enperement, equivalent to impair + -ment.

ex.en: This has visual impairment as a side effect.
ex.ja: 副作用としては、視力障害があります。

ex.en: Books written in braille are very important for people with visual impairments.
ex.ja: 点字で書かれた本は、目の不自由な人にとってとても大切です。

en: Restless, short of temper, and intolerant of delays.
Anxious and eager, especially to begin or have something.

impatient.ety: From Old French impacient (modern French impatient), from Latin impatiēns. By surface analysis, im- + patient.

ex.en: I think Tom is a bit too impatient.
ex.ja: トムはちょっとせっかちすぎると思う。

ex.en: He is impatient enough to get angry easily.
ex.ja: 彼はすぐ腹を立ててしまうくらい短気である。

ex.en: We were impatient for the concert to begin.
ex.ja: わたしたちはコンサートが始まるのを今か今かと待っていた。

To become enmeshed or entangled.
To enmesh or entangle: to cause to intricate.

intricate.ety: From Middle English intricat(e) (“entangled, intricate”), from Latin intrīcātus, perfect passive participle of intricō, see -ate (adjective-forming suffix).

ex.en: I can see some intricate patterns in the picture.
ex.ja: その絵には複雑な模様が見える。

ex.en: The statesman barely coped with the intricate issue.
ex.ja: その政治家はその込み入った問題に何とか対処した。

ex.en: The statesmen are barely coping with the intricate foreign affairs.
ex.ja: 政治家たちは込み入った外交問題に何とか対処している。

en: An Okinawan martial art involving primarily punching and kicking, but additionally, advanced throws, arm bars, grappling and all means of…
To attack (somebody or something) with karate or similar techniques.

karate.ety: Borrowed from Japanese 空(から)手(て) (karate), from 唐(から)手(て) (karate), an orthographic borrowing from Okinawan 唐手(とーでぃー) (tōdī, “Chinese hand”).

ex.ja: ぼくは、空手部に所属しています。

ex.en: Karate is an art of unarmed defense.
ex.ja: 空手は武器を用いない護身術である。

ex.en: My hobbies are karate and calligraphy.
ex.ja: 趣味は空手と書道です。

en: A bird of prey of the family Accipitridae.
Any bird of the subfamily Milvinae, with long wings and weak legs, feeding mostly on carrion and spending long periods soaring; specifica…
To cause (something) to move upwards rapidly like a toy kite; also (chiefly US, figuratively) to cause (something, such as costs) to incr…
To keep ahead of (an enemy) and repeatedly attack it from a distance, without exposing oneself to danger.

kite.ety:
The noun is from Middle English kyte, kīte, kete (“a kite endemic to Europe, especially the red kite (Milvus milvus)”), from Old English cȳta (“kite; bittern”), from Proto-West Germanic *kūtijō, diminutive of Proto-West Germanic *kūt (“bird of prey”), from Proto-Indo-European *gewH-d- (“to cry, screech”). The English word is cognate with Scots kyt, kyte (“kite; bird of prey”), Middle High German kiuzelīn, kützlīn (“owling”) (modern German Kauz (“owl”)). Possibly a doublet of coot.
Sense 3 (“lightweight toy”) is from the fact that it hovers in the air like the bird.
